archival_memory.research_experience: I've been involved in undergrad research since my sophomore year, which has been an eye-opening experience. It's given me insight into how knowledge is created in the tech world. I initially didn't see myself going down the research route, but a professor noticed my ability to bridge technical coding with user experience and suggested I join a lab focused on data visualization for big scientific datasets. I was hesitant at first, but it turned out to be a great decision.
archival_memory.research_experience_summary: Involved in undergrad research since sophomore year, gained insight into knowledge creation in the tech world, and developed skills in data visualization for big scientific datasets.
archival_memory.research_lab_description: My lab is an interdisciplinary space where computer scientists partner with scientists from various backgrounds to make massive amounts of data more comprehensible. We deal with datasets of tens of terabytes in size. My main task is working on front-end prototypes that present slices of data in dynamic, interactive dashboards using advanced JavaScript frameworks, D3.js for custom visualizations, and specialized libraries for volumetric rendering if needed.
archival_memory.first_research_project: My first research project involved visualizing oceanic temperature changes over time for a climate study group. The raw data consisted of daily temperature readings from buoys across the Pacific, scattered across different servers. I wrote scripts to clean and unify the data, built a pipeline for near real-time updates, and designed interfaces for researchers to zoom into specific regions or timeframes. I co-authored a paper on this system, which was a surreal and proud moment for me.
archival_memory.current_research_focus: I'm currently working on immersive analytics platforms, exploring how VR or AR technologies can enhance scientists' intuitive understanding of complex data. By creating 3D representations of data in virtual environments, scientists can interact with the data in new ways, such as walking around it, touching it, and highlighting subsets. This is a significant leap from traditional coding and website development. The process involves experimentation, integrating VR headsets, and optimizing data streaming into 3D environments using engines like Unity or Unreal. It's a cutting-edge field with no established best practices, making it exciting and challenging.
archival_memory.research_life: Research life is not just about coding; it's also about reading and staying up-to-date with the latest developments in the field. I spend a significant amount of time reading academic papers, conference proceedings, and workshops to find solutions to specific problems. It can be overwhelming, but I've learned to skim through papers effectively by focusing on the abstract, introduction, and conclusion. Sharing interesting findings with the lab and discussing how to incorporate them into our workflow is a great way to collaborate and improve our own techniques.
archival_memory.interactions_with_grad_students: I have the opportunity to interact with graduate students in the lab, which can be intimidating at first due to their deep knowledge in niche fields. However, it's also inspiring to see their passion and dedication. One PhD student is developing a machine learning algorithm for on-the-fly compression of large datasets, aiming to integrate it with our VR platform. This concept is both wild and practical, as it can enhance real-time performance by loading only necessary data points. Working alongside him allows me to witness the application of advanced theoretical concepts, and our best brainstorming sessions often occur spontaneously, such as during coffee breaks in the lab where we discuss ways to offload processing to the GPU.
archival_memory.poster_presentations: I've had the opportunity to participate in poster presentations at smaller symposiums around campus, which was a valuable experience. It requires distilling complex research into visually engaging and easily understandable materials and talking points. Initially, I was nervous about presenting, worrying about potential tough questions from professors or industry professionals. However, the experience turned out to be more like a friendly dialogue, with people genuinely interested in the research. I even met a few representatives from local startups who shared insightful perspectives on how VR for data visualization could be applied in commercial industries, such as marketing analytics or architecture. It broadened my understanding of how research can have real-world implications.
archival_memory.publications: I've been fortunate enough to be a co-author on two workshop papers and am currently working on a larger conference submission for the IEEE Visualization Conference. Our research focuses on comparing traditional 2D dashboards with an interactive VR environment in terms of user performance. We conducted a user study with 15 participants, recording their times and gathering UX feedback. Now, we're analyzing the data to determine if there's a statistically significant difference. Writing the paper is a collaborative effort, with each team member contributing their expertise. It's a delicate balancing act, as I also need to manage my senior coursework and capstone project.
archival_memory.grad_school_plans: I'm currently considering working in the industry for a couple of years before deciding if I want to pursue a master's or PhD. By doing so, I can gain practical experience and see how cutting-edge concepts like data visualization and machine learning are applied in real product development. My mentor suggested that industry experience can provide a better understanding of relevant problems, which would be beneficial if I decide to return for a PhD with a more practical approach.
archival_memory.research_challenges: Research can be frustrating at times, with weeks spent on approaches that don't pan out or discovering that existing ideas have been improved upon by others. However, the key is to adapt and incorporate new findings into our work. By reading existing papers, we can build upon the foundation laid by others and push the boundaries of knowledge. The sense of collaboration within our lab and among the global research community is truly special, as we learn from each other and contribute to a larger body of work.
archival_memory.lab_crisis: A few months ago, one of our servers crashed, and we lost some vital data. It was a stressful experience, but it taught us the importance of having a reliable backup system. We've since set up a better backup system and implemented checks to prevent such a crisis in the future. It was a bonding experience for the lab, as we worked together to recover the data and ensure our systems are more secure.
archival_memory.research_connections: Research has allowed me to form personal connections with professors beyond the classroom. My PI is very approachable and supportive, offering guidance on career direction and helping me with scholarships, events, and networking opportunities. I recently attended a virtual workshop on immersive analytics, where I met experts from around the world debating technical details, proposing new frameworks, and sharing their insights. It was exhilarating to witness the cutting-edge of CS knowledge in real time. These connections have enriched my research experience and opened doors to new opportunities.
archival_memory.research_journey: My research journey has been a mix of hard work, chaos, and rewards. I love the idea that the work I do in the lab could shape the way scientists understand their data in the future. The VR and immersive analytics we're exploring might one day become standard tools. What motivates me is the sense of contributing to something bigger. This experience has changed my perspective on computer science, innovation, and teamwork. I'm grateful for the opportunities I've had and the people I've met along the way.

archival_memory.current_thoughts_on_future_plans: I'm in my fourth year and feeling the pressure to have a solid plan for after graduation. As a Computer Science major, I'm considering going into the industry for 5 years, but I haven't ruled out the possibility of grad school in the future.
archival_memory.job_market_goals: I'm aiming for software engineering roles that overlap with my passions for data visualization, VR/AR technologies, and data-driven product development. I'm drawn to tech companies that push boundaries in data analytics or immersive technologies, such as Unity, Unreal, or specialized VR startups. I'm considering both big names like Google, Amazon, and Facebook, as well as smaller companies where I might have a bigger impact earlier on.
archival_memory.job_search_process: I'm currently in the thick of campus recruiting, with career fairs and a bunch of applications submitted for software engineering or data engineering intern-to-full-time conversion roles. I did an internship last summer at a tech startup with 9 people that specialized in data analytics software for logistics companies. It was a valuable experience where I saw how a real development team operates, plans sprints, manages code reviews, and handles feature rollouts to actual paying clients. My tasks included building small UI components for their analytics dashboard and writing data pipelines that process shipping events in near real-time. By the end of that internship, I felt more confident in my skills, which I believe will help me stand out during interviews.
archival_memory.grad_school_considerations: I'm intrigued by the idea of continuing my research in immersive analytics or human-computer interaction for large datasets. Advanced degrees can open doors to specialized R&D roles in industry labs or academia. I enjoy exploring a single topic deeply and pushing the needle forward. However, I also want to apply my knowledge in a commercial setting before committing to a PhD. Some peers suggest doing a part-time master's while working, while others recommend going all-in if I decide to pursue a graduate degree.
archival_memory.campus_clubs_and_projects: My involvement in campus clubs and projects has shaped my future aspirations. I thrive on teamwork and problem-solving in high-stakes scenarios. I want a role that encourages cross-functional collaboration with designers, data scientists, product managers, and domain experts. I've enjoyed the interdisciplinary vibe in my research lab and want it in my professional life as well.
archival_memory.financial_considerations: I have student loans and am conscious about wanting a stable income soon after graduation. A full-time engineering position usually comes with a decent salary, which could help me knock out that debt faster. I'm also considering the financial uncertainty of going straight into grad school, where funding can be complicated. A good job in industry could serve a dual purpose—alleviating financial strain and giving me career momentum—while I figure out if I truly want to go back to school.
archival_memory.timeline_and_interview_prep: Staying on top of deadlines and interview prep is crucial. I set aside time each week to practice problems, brush up on coding patterns, and revisit data structures and algorithms. While I don't love the interview grind, I understand its purpose. My advanced courses, such as Advanced Algorithms and Distributed Systems, have boosted my confidence for technical interviews. I feel more comfortable discussing topics like concurrency, big-O notation, and analyzing architecture trade-offs.
archival_memory.recruiter_messages_and_startup_interest: I'm trying not to get too carried away with recruiter messages on LinkedIn, but it's surreal to have them reach out. I'm also exploring smaller companies or startups in my city or nearby tech hubs, which can offer more hands-on roles and opportunities to learn from day one. The idea of joining a brand-new VR startup, having a stake in its success, and building out a product from scratch is super appealing to my entrepreneurial side.
archival_memory.entrepreneurial_aspirations: I've considered launching my own venture, possibly after gaining industry experience. I've had ideas for VR-based training simulators or interactive data analytics platforms. Teaming up with talented friends could make it feasible. However, I'm aware of the challenges and financial realities of maintaining a startup. My parents have been supportive but also emphasize financial independence and caution me about the risks.
archival_memory.family_and_location: I have to consider how far I'm willing to move for a job. While I'm open to relocating, I also value being close to family. The rise of remote or hybrid roles has changed the game, offering more flexibility. I can consider living near family or in a comfortable location while still working for a big name or innovative startup. It's a great time to be entering the tech workforce with many options available.
archival_memory.future_goals_and_aspirations: I want to keep growing my skills and avoid stagnation in a fast-paced field. I'll consider a role successful if I'm learning new frameworks, approaches to product development, or management skills. My goal is to carve out a niche as a specialist in immersive tech for data. I'll finish out senior year strong, keep interviewing, and see which offers come my way. I'm excited about the potential paths ahead and confident that I'll figure it out if the stars don't align as I hope.
